back: The current at time t across a cross-section is the value of the ratio delta_Q/delta_t in the limit delta_t tending to zero: I = lim (delta_t -> 0) delta_Q/delta_t.
I = q/t, where q = q+ - q- is the net charge crossing the area in the forward direction in time t. A negative value means the current is in the backward direction.
SI unit is the ampere (A), defined through the magnetic effects of currents.
V is proportional to I, or V = R I, where R is the resistance of the conductor. Units of R: ohm (V/A).
R = rho l / A. Doubling the length doubles R; halving the area doubles R; rho depends on the material only.
j = I/A, current per unit area normal to the flow. SI unit A m^-2, dimensions [L^-2 A].
E = rho j, equivalently j = sigma E with sigma = 1/rho the conductivity. Both are equivalent to V = R I.
v_d = -e E tau / m, where tau is the relaxation time. The drift velocity is independent of time even though the electrons are accelerated.
I = n e A v_d, where n is the free-electron number density and A the cross-section. In vector form j = n e v_d.
sigma = n e^2 tau / m, and rho = m / (n e^2 tau). Ohm's law follows if n and tau are independent of E.
The average time between two successive collisions of a free electron with the ions. Symbol tau, SI unit s, dimensions [T].
mu = |v_d| / E = e tau / m. SI unit m^2 V^-1 s^-1; it is 10^4 times the value in cm^2 V^-1 s^-1. Mobility is positive.

front: Why drift speed is so small
back: For 1.5 A in a copper wire of 1.0 x 10^-7 m^2 and n = 8.5 x 10^28 m^-3, v_d is about 1.1 mm/s - roughly 10^5 times smaller than the thermal speed and 10^11 times smaller than the speed of the electric field.

front: Three ways Ohm's law can fail
back: (a) V not proportional to I; (b) the V-I relation depends on the sign of V (diode); (c) the relation is not unique (GaAs).
Metals 10^-8 to 10^-6 ohm m; insulators (ceramic, rubber, plastics) about 10^18 times larger or more; semiconductors in between, on a log scale.
rho_T = rho_0 [1 + alpha (T - T_0)] over a limited range. alpha is the temperature coefficient of resistivity, dimension (Temperature)^-1, positive for metals.

front: Why rho rises for metals but falls for semiconductors
back: rho = m/(n e^2 tau). In metals n is fixed and tau falls with T, so rho rises. In semiconductors n rises with T and more than compensates the fall in tau, so rho falls.
Nichrome (Ni, Fe, Cr), manganin and constantan have a very weak temperature dependence of resistivity, so they are used for wire-bound standard resistors.
delta_W = I V delta_t; power P = I V = I^2 R = V^2 / R (ohmic loss). The energy comes from the source - for a cell, its chemical energy.
P_c = I^2 R_c = P^2 R_c / V^2. To deliver a given power with minimum loss, transmit at a very high V; transformers lower the voltage at the consumer end.
emf = V+ + V- > 0 - the potential difference between the electrodes in an open circuit. It is a potential difference, not a force.
V = emf - I r, where r is the internal resistance. Equivalently I = emf/(R + r) and V_ext = emf R/(R + r); the maximum current is emf/r at R = 0.
emf_eq = e1 + e2 and r_eq = r1 + r2. If a cell is reversed, its emf enters with a negative sign: emf_eq = e1 - e2 (e1 > e2).
1/r_eq = 1/r1 + 1/r2 and emf_eq/r_eq = e1/r1 + e2/r2, i.e. emf_eq = (e1 r2 + e2 r1)/(r1 + r2) and r_eq = r1 r2/(r1 + r2).

Junction rule: sum of currents in = sum out (conservation of charge). Loop rule: algebraic sum of potential changes round a closed loop is zero. Wheatstone balance: R2/R1 = R4/R3, i.e. R1/R2 = R3/R4, when the galvanometer current is zero.
